_orphan_predicate_under_test: category == "" AND the torrent is genuinely complete AND its bytes are at rest

samples._label: THE HAPPY PATH — uncategorised, complete, seeding, multi-file with a root folder
samples.name: The.Matrix.1999.1080p.BluRay.x264-AMIABLE

samples._label: CATEGORISED — Sonarr owns this. Must be skipped even though it is complete.
samples.name: Show.Name.S01E01.1080p.WEB-DL.x264-GRP

samples._label: TRAP: SINGLE-FILE TORRENT — content_path is a FILE, not a directory
samples._trap: torrentimpl.cpp contentPath(): if filesCount()==1 it returns actualStorageLocation()/filePath(0). Any code that does os.listdir(content_path) or treats it as a release folder breaks here.
samples.name: Show.Name.S01E01.1080p.WEB.mkv

samples._label: TRAP: MULTI-FILE TORRENT WITH NO COMMON ROOT FOLDER — content_path == save_path
samples._trap: Path::findRootFolder() returns empty when any file sits at the top level, so contentPath() falls back to actualStorageLocation(). content_path is then the ENTIRE completed directory, shared with every other torrent. Moving or deleting it is catastrophic. Orphanarr MUST compare content_path against save_path and refuse (or fall back to per-file handling) when they are equal.
samples.name: Some Loose Files

samples._label: TRAP: completion_on == -1 on a fully complete torrent
samples._trap: Utils::DateTime::toSecsSinceEpoch() returns -1 for an invalid QDateTime, and m_completedTime is only set when libtorrent reports completed_time > 0. Torrents adopted from a migrated client — exactly the population Orphanarr targets — routinely have no completion time. Any 'wait N hours after completion' rule keyed on completion_on will either never fire or fire immediately. Use added_on or first-seen-by-Orphanarr instead.
samples.name: Migrated.Release.2011.720p.BluRay.x264-GRP

samples._label: TRAP: progress == 1 but the torrent is being rechecked
samples._trap: state 'checkingUP' means libtorrent is reading every piece. progress/amount_left alone say 'done'. Acting now races the recheck.
samples.name: Rechecking.Release.2020.1080p

samples._label: TRAP: state 'moving' — qBittorrent is relocating the data right now
samples._trap: content_path is derived from actualStorageLocation() = libtorrent's current save_path, which is mid-flight. The path Orphanarr reads will be wrong seconds later.
samples.name: Relocating.Release.2020.1080p

samples._label: TRAP: partially-downloaded torrent with unwanted files deselected
samples._trap: progress is 1 and amount_left is 0 because progress is computed over WANTED bytes only. size (wanted) < total_size (all files). The release folder on disk is incomplete relative to the .torrent. Orphanarr must plan from the actual files on disk, not from the torrent's declared file list.
samples.name: Season.Pack.S01.1080p.WEB-DL

samples._label: TRAP: magnet link with no metadata yet
samples._trap: contentPath() and rootPath() both return an EMPTY string when hasMetadata() is false. An empty content_path joined onto a destination root yields the destination root itself.
samples.name: 6f3b1c1e2d4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c

samples._label: TRAP: tags are joined with ', ' — comma AND space
samples._trap: serialize_torrent.cpp: Utils::String::joinIntoString(torrent.tags(), u", "_s). The wiki says 'comma-concatenated'. A naive split(',') leaves a leading space on every tag after the first, so an exclusion list keyed on 'orphanarr-ignore' silently never matches ' orphanarr-ignore'.
samples.name: Tagged.Release.2020.1080p

samples._label: TRAP: stopped/paused naming changed in qBittorrent 5.x
samples._trap: qBittorrent <5.0 emitted 'pausedUP'/'pausedDL'. Master emits 'stoppedUP'/'stoppedDL' (serialize_torrent.cpp). The published WebUI-API-(qBittorrent-5.0) wiki page STILL documents the paused names. Any completeness test built from an allow-list of state strings must accept both spellings.
samples.name: Stopped.Release.2020.1080p

samples._label: TRAP: errored / missing-files torrent that still reports progress 1
samples._trap: The user already deleted or moved the data. content_path points at nothing. Orphanarr must stat the path before planning anything.
samples.name: Vanished.Release.2020.1080p

samples._label: TRAP: category is whitespace, not empty
samples._trap: Session::isValidCategoryName rejects most junk, but a category can legitimately contain a '/' for subcategories (e.g. 'movies/4k'). Do not assume category is a flat token, and do not treat a non-empty-but-odd category as uncategorised.
samples.name: Subcategorised.Release.2020.1080p
